lines: Good morning my love. If you need any heavy lifting done on the farm today, just say the word.
$1Consider it an official request.
You're back late. I was tempted to bring you home...
$1Come, sit down. Tell me about your day.
Being your partner in this quiet valley... it is a victory I never sought,
$4yet it is the greatest one I have.
This space is... peaceful. I am unaccustomed to luxury,
$2but a soldier appreciates a well-maintained base of operations. Not to brag but...
$4I get to wake up beside the best view in the entire valley everyday.
I tried to feed the chickens.
$7They completely ignored my authority!
$5I suppose my presence isn't very... vexing to a flock of birds.
$7It was... humbling.
The rain reminds me of the storms over Midgar,
$2but there is no acid in this water. It is just... nature.
$6Stay inside today if you can. I do not wish for you to catch a cold.
My movements are... slowing down.
$8Not from age! it's because the edge is gone!
$1I no longer feel the need to destroy. I only feel the urge to protect this land.
$6To protect you.
$1Good morning, {{playerName}}. I brewed fresh tea while you were still asleep—I hope it is to your liking.
$3Once, my mornings began with briefings and steel. Waking up to sunlight on the floorboards and the sound of your breathing is a peace I still struggle to put into words.
$8You were already out the door before dawn yesterday. Even a SOLDIER needs proper rest, {{playerName}}.
$6Promise me you will pause for a proper meal at midday. If you will not slow down for your own sake, do it for mine.
$1I found a volume on local botany in the bookshelf earlier. It is remarkable how much life thrives here without interference.
$3Whenever you come back inside, the book immediately loses my attention—though I suppose I do not mind that at all.
$0Sometimes I catch myself simply standing in the kitchen, listening to the clock tick.
$2There are no emergencies waiting beyond the door. No voices calling me away.
$1Only a quiet home, and the person who gave me a second chance at life. Have a safe day out there, {{playerName}}.
$1I tidied the entryway and checked the pantry stores this morning. Everything is in order.
$1Whenever your work is done, come straight back to me. I will be waiting.
The rain against the roof used to remind me of long, bleak campaigns far from home.
$1Now, listening to it while watching you move about the farmhouse... it is the most soothing sound in the world.
The mud along the southern path looks treacherous today. Mind your footing out there, {{playerName}}.
$1If you come back chilled to the bone, I will have warm towels and hot broth waiting by the hearth.
$8You are soaked through, {{playerName}}. Come step closer to the fire before you catch a chill.
$1Let the storm rage outside all it wishes—nothing can touch us within these walls.
On nights like this, old memories occasionally knock at the door... yet they no longer hold any power over me.
$4One glance at you, {{playerName}}, and all the shadows scatter. Thank you for being my anchor.
$1I walked the perimeter of the fields earlier. Everything is quiet, save for the wind in the crops.
$1To nurture life from the soil rather than take it... I think I finally understand why you love this work so much.
$0Do not mind me—I was only taking in the fresh air.
$1Though I will admit, watching you tend the farm is far more captivating than the scenery.
$1The mountain air clears the mind wonderfully.
$1I was just reflecting on how far we have come since the day I first arrived in this valley. Whatever lies ahead, {{playerName}}, I am grateful to walk it beside you.
$1Welcome home, {{playerName}}. You look exhausted—let me take care of the rest of the evening.
$1Set your tools aside and rest for a while. You do not have to carry every burden on your own anymore.
$1...I'll imagine we fell in love. I'll nap under moonlight skies with you...
$3...I think I'll picture us, you with the waves. The ocean's colors on your face...
$4...I'll leave my heart with your air. So let me fly with you...
$4...Will you be forever with me?... (He keeps singing 'Blue' by Yung Kai)
If I were given the chance to rewrite my past, I would hesitate—not because I do not regret the pain I caused, but because every winding road eventually led me to your door.
$3I love you, {{playerName}}. More deeply than I ever thought a man like me was capable of loving.
$1...when you said Tulips. I knew that you're mine...
$3...When I caught you there, crying in the night...
$1...Wearing my jacket, wearing that smile...
$6...I knew that I'd found you...
$1...Were you unawares? Did it catch you out?...
$1...Or did it break you in right from the start?...
$1...This is pure as fire, this is pure as snow...
$3...I knew that I'd found you...
$1...This could be an opportunity...
$1...If you promise to let it grow...
$3This... was the song you reminded me of when you gifted me Tulips. A song by Bloc Party that reminds me of you. Tulips...
$3'Cause you're the one I love!
$1...Boys workin' on empty... Is that the kinda way to face the burning heat?...
$3...I just think about my baby. I'm so full of love I could barely eat...
$3...There's nothing sweeter than my baby. I'd never want once from the cherry tree
$3...Cause my baby's sweet as can be...
$4...She'd give me toothaches just from kissin' me...
$0...When... my... time comes around...
$1...Lay me gently in the cold dark earth...
$1...No grave... can hold my body down...
$3...I'll crawl home to her...
(He kisses {{playerName}}'s cheek and keeps singing 'Work Song' by Hozier)
...When I was young, before we begun...
$1...I never thought we all had someone...
$1...I took your breath but you took the rest...
$3...I promised you always... a place on my chest...
...There might come a day...
$2...When you feel that I'm not who I was...
$4...You might find a better one... and end it for us...
...So I wrote... our... days on our... kitchen table...
$6...If you ever forget... that you love me...
$4(He avoids your gaze continues singing 'If you ever forget that you love me' by Isak Danielson)
$1...I had a thought, dear. However scary. About that night, the bugs and the dirt...
$2...Why were you digging? What did you bury. Before those hands pulled me, From the earth?...
$1...I will not ask you where you came from. I will not ask you, neither should you...

$3Is it silly to say you've turned me into a whimsical man? This life is surreal to me. I find it so... peaceful and free'ing... I find myself drawn to things I would never have dreamed of since you've come to Stardew Valley.
$1You've brought song into my life {{playerName}}
And so I will sing those songs for you. I heard one of your favorites was 'Like real people do' by Hozier, and so...
$3...Honey just put your sweet lips on my lips. We should just kiss like real people do...
$1...I wanna get to Heaven. Baby, tell me what to do...
...I'm scared this is ending. Expose the lies from the truth...
$2...Will I ever get to Heaven? I'd go through Hell for you...
$6...Can we keep on transcending? Or maybe I'm just meant to lose...
$4...Maybe I'm just meant to lose you... (He avoids your gaze as he reflects on the bittersweet lyrics by David Kushner's "I wanna get to heaven")
$4...Forgive me. I did not hear you walk in.
$6The storm felt a little too heavy today, so I found myself humming an old melody to keep my thoughts from drifting too far back.
$3However... seeing you always brings me right back to the present, {{playerName}}. Thank you for bringing the quiet to the storm today.
Rain has a way of washing the color out of everything, leaving only the memories you try not to examine too closely.
$2There are days I still wonder how a man with my past was permitted to end up somewhere this gentle.
$4...Stay safe out there today, {{playerName}}. Knowing you will come back through that door is the only thing that quiets the noise.
Once, I knew nothing of seasons—only campaigns, ash, and the next horizon to conquer.
$2Standing here watching rain nourish crops I helped plant... it feels almost like watching a stranger's life.
$4A good life, {{playerName}}. Even if part of me still feels like a ghost borrowing someone else's warmth.
On nights when the rain beats against the glass like this, it is easy to remember everyone I failed... and everyone I hurt.
$2I cannot undo the past, {{playerName}}. No amount of quiet days here will ever erase it.
$1Yet when you sit beside me in the dark and hold my hand without flinching... it feels enough to simply try to be better tomorrow.
$0Listen... to the rain on the eaves... It is strange how something so dreary outside can make a single room feel like the entire world.
$2Sometimes I look at you in the firelight and feel a sudden fear that I will wake up back in the dark, and none of this was real.
$4Stay close tonight, {{playerName}}. Remind me I am really here.
The storm shows no sign of letting up before dawn.
$1Let the rain wash away whatever remains of yesterday. Tomorrow is another chance to live as a better man than the one I was.
$1Come to bed when you are ready, {{playerName}}. I will keep the dark at bay until morning.
$2I am not much for conversation tonight, {{playerName}}. The weather has left my thoughts rather heavy.
$0You need not say anything to fix it. Simply sitting beside you while the storm passes is more comfort than I deserve.
$1Once, I measured my worth solely by the edge of a blade and the fear in other men's eyes.
$4Now, my proudest accomplishment is seeing you smile over morning coffee, {{playerName}}.
$3It is a gentler kind of strength... and I am grateful every day that you taught me how to hold it.
$2There are still moments when old regrets feel heavy, {{playerName}}—ghosts do not vanish overnight.
$1Yet the moment I hear your footsteps on the porch, the weight simply lifts.
$3You have become my sanctuary. Whatever you need of me today, name it. Whatever it is, it is yours. Now and evermore.
I caught myself humming earlier while sweeping the porch—something I have not done since my earliest days as a cadet, long before everything went wrong.
$1I suppose happiness sneaks up on a man when he is not looking, {{playerName}}. Thank you for giving me a reason to sing again.
You have been working yourself far too hard lately, {{playerName}}.
$1Come here for just a moment... Let me hold you before you rush back out into the fields. Even the valley can wait five minutes.
Forgive me if I seem overly quiet today. My thoughts have simply been wandering through old memories.
$6I am well, {{playerName}}—truly. Take care of yourself out there.
Ah... {{playerName}}. I did not expect you to stop and speak with me today.
$8If I have done something to disappoint you, tell me plainly. I would rather face the truth than guess at shadows.
$2The farmhouse is in order. You need not concern yourself with me.
$5I am well accustomed to solitude, {{playerName}}. Do whatever it is you need to do.
$2The silence in this house feels very different than it did when we first wed... heavier, somehow.
$4I do not know how to mend a rift without a sword, {{playerName}}. Tell me what I am doing wrong.
$3I have been organizing a few mementos and volumes I managed to salvage from my travels.
$1It is strange seeing the remnants of my old life resting beneath a peaceful farmhouse roof... yet nothing here feels threatening anymore.
$3Make yourself at home in here whenever you wish, {{playerName}}. There are no secrets left between us.
$1I thought I might take a quiet walk toward the mountain lake and the forest edge today.
$3Old habits—I still feel the need to stretch my legs and observe the horizon from time to time.
$1Do not worry, {{playerName}}. I will be back before sundown.
$1I had a pleasant walk today. Gunther and I spoke briefly about ancient history, and Linus offered me some wild berries along the path.
$4It still marvels me how easily this town accepts my presence... though coming back through our front door remains the best part of my day, {{playerName}}.
$1I prepared something warm for you before you head out into the fields today.
$3Please take care of yourself, {{playerName}}. Your well-being means everything to me.
I rose early and watered the crops for you this morning, {{playerName}}.
There is something deeply calming about tending to growing things. Consider it a small token of my gratitude.
$4When I first held %kid1, my hands were actually trembling—not out of fear, {{playerName}}, but from the sheer weight of wanting to protect someone so small.
$2I spent my entire life wielding a blade meant to end lives.
$4To nurture a new one instead... I never dreamed I would be trusted with such a gift.
$1%kid1 was restless earlier, so I walked the hallway humming an old lullaby until they drifted off.
$3It seems my voice is better suited to putting children to sleep than giving orders on a battlefield. I cannot say I mind.
$3Watching %kid1 play on the rug without a single worry in the world...
$8I never had a real childhood of my own, {{playerName}}. Everything was training, tests, and expectations from the very beginning.
$4Seeing our child grow up safe, warm, and deeply loved mends a part of me I thought was beyond repair.
$3Do not worry about the house today, {{playerName}}. I have already fed %kid1 and checked every corner of the nursery twice.
$7Nothing in this valley—or any other world—will ever harm a hair on their head while I am standing watch!
$8This farmhouse used to be as quiet as an empty barracks. Now, between %kid1 and %kid2, there is scarcely a silent moment all day.
$3Yet I would not trade a single footstep or laugh for all the quiet in the world, {{playerName}}.
$6Watching %kid1 look out for %kid2 earlier brought a lump to my throat.
$5Family used to be nothing more than a word in a Shinra file to me.
$4Looking at the two of them—and looking at you, {{playerName}}—I finally understand what it truly means.
$1%kid1 insisted on showing me a shiny pebble earlier, while %kid2 tried to tug on my coat at the exact same moment.
$3I have faced entire armies without breaking a sweat, {{playerName}}, yet two toddlers nearly managed to outflank me before breakfast.
$1Sometimes at night, after %kid1 and %kid2 are fast asleep, I stand in the doorway just listening to them breathe.
$1No war. No voices in the dark. Just a warm house, two children who know nothing but kindness, and the woman who made it all possible.
$4Thank you for everything, {{playerName}}.
